documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost for Education (AI Council)
documents.title: Tufts Generative AI Usage Guidelines for Faculty, Staff, and Students
documents.stance_why: The guidelines call themselves "deliberately non-prescriptive" and say "Faculty have the freedom and responsibility to determine appropriate AI use within their courses", noting faculty "may require AI use, permit it with conditions, discourage it, or prohibit it." They set no default rule, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: Tufts' university-wide guidelines, adopted by the AI Council in spring 2026, set six principles (accountability, ethical responsibility, community trust, transparency, clarifying AI use, course expectations). They are deliberately non-prescriptive: instructors decide what AI use is allowed and should communicate it, and everyone should disclose substantive use and protect restricted data.

units.anchor: AI systems can reflect stereotypes, omit perspectives, or make overconfident claims

units.why: "Don't enter sensitive personal information, confidential data, or proprietary course materials into public AI tools": data privacy (P50), also covering course materials (P49 as alternative).
units.anchor: Don't enter sensitive personal information, confidential data, or proprietary course materials into public AI tools
units.fit_note: Also bars proprietary course materials (P49).

units.why: Says documenting AI use is an "important professional practice" and norms "continually evolv[e]"; a reason for disclosure, P24 with note.
units.anchor: Documenting AI use is an important professional practice, though norms are continually evolving
units.fit_note: Rationale for disclosure; also notes norms evolve (P54).

units.why: "if AI influenced your thinking, structure, or content in any substantive way, document it", P24.
units.anchor: if AI influenced your thinking, structure, or content in any substantive way, document it

units.why: "Routine spell-check doesn't require documentation" exempts routine features, P100; it adds to over-document when unsure.
units.anchor: Routine spell-check doesn't require documentation
units.fit_note: Also says over-document when unsure.

units.why: Students "add an AI Acknowledgment" for each assignment with AI beyond routine checks, P24.
units.anchor: add an AI Acknowledgment that includes

units.why: The acknowledgment names the "Tool(s) used", P25.
units.anchor: Tool(s) used

units.why: The acknowledgment states "How you used it" with a debugging example, P25.
units.anchor: How you used it

units.why: The acknowledgment states "How you evaluated/modified the output", a short reflection, P26.
units.anchor: How you evaluated/modified the output
units.fit_note: A short note rather than full transcripts.

units.why: "Place any AI-generated text in quotation marks with attribution" marks AI text where it appears, P27.
units.anchor: Place any AI-generated text in quotation marks with attribution
units.fit_note: Applies to AI-generated text.

units.why: Points students to an "AI Fluency course" and office hours for AI skills: AI-literacy training for students, P70.
units.anchor: explore resources like Anthropic's AI Fluency course or discuss strategies in office hours

units.why: School of Nutrition example: "the use of AI is encouraged to enhance your learning", default encouraging, P02.
units.anchor: the use of AI is encouraged to enhance your learning

units.why: Hopes students "adopt a growth mindset around AI, continuously exploring new technologies and best practices", staying informed, P102.
units.anchor: adopt a growth mindset around AI, continuously exploring new technologies and best practices

units.why: Students may use AI to "deepen your understanding ... brainstorm, get feedback, synthesize, revise and/or edit", a broad list of permitted uses. Assigned to P12 (understanding materials) as lead.
units.anchor: use AI tools to deepen your understanding of learning materials, brainstorm, get feedback, synthesize, revise
units.fit_note: Covers several permitted uses at once: understanding, brainstorming, feedback, revising, editing.

units.why: "AI is a supporting tool rather than a replacement for human creativity and critical thinking", AI must not replace students' thinking, P32.
units.anchor: AI is a supporting tool rather than a replacement for human creativity and critical thinking

units.why: Submitting AI-generated work as own "is a violation of Tufts Academic Integrity policies", P36.
units.anchor: Submitting any work generated by an AI program as your own is a violation of

units.why: "Specific recommendations on how to use or not use AI on each assignment", assignment-level rules, P04.
units.anchor: There are specific recommendations on how to use or not use AI on each assignment

units.why: Students should "familiarize yourself with how AI works and its limitations"; closest is P31 (output can be wrong), though it also asks for learning how AI works.
units.anchor: Familiarize yourself with how AI works and its limitations, including bias and production of false
units.fit_note: Also asks students to learn how AI works, not only to verify output.

units.why: "Identify and cite the AI tools you use" and include a conversation link if available, citing tool and output, P25.
units.anchor: Identify and cite the AI tools you use

units.why: Students must "be transparent about how you used it" with an acknowledgment section or footnotes, P24.
units.anchor: Be transparent about how you used it, and include an acknowledgment section and/or as footnotes

units.why: Links to a worksheet "to help clarify AI boundaries for specific assignments", a resource for faculty setting expectations, P63.
units.anchor: A tool to help clarify AI boundaries for specific assignments

units.why: Links to the AI Assessment Scale, a framework of levels of AI use in assessment, P05.
units.anchor: A practical framework to guide the appropriate and ethical use of generative AI in assessment

units.why: Links to a blog post "reviewing research on AI and learning", evidence on AI's effects on learning, P55.
units.anchor: Teaching@Tufts blog post reviewing research on AI and learning

notes: The CELT page embeds example policies from individual Tufts courses and hypothetical templates; their units are coded under the page's university layer, and unit_stance reflects each example's own position. The Intro to Computation for Engineers example says Tufts has no institution-wide AI policy, which predates the Spring 2026 guidelines. A few sentences are coded as more than one unit when they hold distinct rules.
